subject: lavaan estimation one or two stage?

messages.author: 20a091f3d0e9ee8f
messages.subject: lavaan estimation one or two stage?
parts:
Dear all,

when you fit a model using sem(), in the background the optimizer estimate first the measurement model and then the structural model? or just both at once?

Thank you!

Michael.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: lavaan estimation one or two stage?
parts:
The sem()  functions (and related: cfa, lavaan) estimate both parts of the model simultaneously.  The recently released sam() [structural after measurement] function fits the measurement part first and the structural part afterwards. See, for example, https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/sam.html or https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2023-15946-001 .

Jeremy

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan estimation one or two stage?
parts:
On 4/20/25 09:14, Michael Filsecker wrote:
> thank you for your reply. I wonder when using the example data
> "Industrialization and Political Democrycy" with SAM and then with the
> "old" Sem() in lavaan, what differences do we have to expect?

For the structural part, the results will be very similar (if not
identical) IF you use a single measurement block that includes all the
three latent variables, like this:

fit.sam <- sam(model, data = PoliticalDemocracy, mm.list = list(joint =
c("ind60", "dem60", "dem65")))

Per default, sam() will fit a one-factor CFA per latent variable; for
the political democracy example, that is not a good idea, as dem60 and
dem65 are 'linked', and should be fitted together, as shown in the
example of the man page of sam().

Yves.

--
Yves Rosseel
Department of Data Analysis, Ghent University
